drivers.variant_notes: Earliest L-1 game ROMs (cycl_u26.l1, cycl_u27.l1) on the same game data and sound ROMs. Its U27 name tables decode to the L-5 text at the same offsets, and its Coil Test steps the same 28 pulses with the same names (runtime evidence).

Earlier L-4 game ROMs (cycl_u26.l4, cycl_u27.l4) on the same game data and sound ROMs. Its U27 name tables decode to the L-5 text at the same offsets, and its Coil Test steps the same 28 pulses with the same names (runtime evidence).

Production L-5 game ROMs (cycl_u26.l5, cycl_u27.l5), the known-working script's cGameName. All three drivers select the same cyclnGameData (GEN_S11B, s11_dispS11b1, A/C relay 12, FLIP_SWNO(57,58)) and the same U21/U22 and U4/U19 sound ROMs; only the U26 and U27 game ROMs differ. Every service, mechanism and gameplay run was made on this ROM.

The Switches list footnotes the part (5490-10159-00 Mystery Wheel Opto) as "Part of Motor Control Assy, D-12046", and the Switch-Matrix Table places it on the backbox insert board; the parts manual lists the 5490-10159-00 Opto Interruptor Module as Opto 1 of the D-12045 Mystery Wheel Opto Positioner board, the stepper motor control assembly of the C-12036 carousel, and service bulletin SS47 lists D-12046 as a subassembly of that D-12045 Stepper Control Assembly, so both numbers name the same board. Its schematic draws the opto switching the matrix row and column pins through a transistor (Q9) rather than as a contact. In the Mystery Wheel Test the ROM shows "H" on the player 4 display while 41 is 0 and no "H" while it is 1 (runs wheel-test-41-0 and wheel-test-41-1); the manual says "H" means the home switch is open or the opto is interrupted. A rising edge of 41 restarted the step count (run wheel-test-reactive). The retained script's cvpmMech (.Length = 200, .Steps = 360, lines 78-79) closes 41 while its reported position is 0-180 of 360, half a turn (line 80). In the ROM's Switch Levels test (run switch-levels) holding public 41 at 1 alone made the player 1 and 2 displays show "M. WHEEL H. OPTO" and the player 3 display 06 41, so the ROM reads it active at 1. pia4a_r returns core_getSwCol without inversion and the driver declares no inverted switch, so the contact the matrix sees is open at rest and closed when actuated.

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(57,58) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

System 11's single Country jumper, read as core_getDip(0)<<7 on PIA2 PA7, which pinned s11.c labels "Jumper W7". The manual's ROM and Jumper Table lists W7 among the CPU board's installed jumpers (W1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 14, 16, 17, and 19). pia2a_r is an eight-bit handler, so only bit 0 of the host value reaches PA7: every retained run used 0 and the ROM ran its English service text. The retained script sets .DIP(0) = &H80 (line 61), which shifts to 0x4000 and reaches PA7 as 0, the same as 0.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball rests on the outhole switch (10, 17-1067) and the Outhole Kicker (1, AE-23-800) kicks it out; the ball is served to the shooter lane, whose switch (25, 5647-12073-04) it rests on until plunged. The matrix has no ball-trough switch and the Solenoid Table no ball-release coil, so the outhole kick is the only serve the CPU controls; the playfield underside drawing labels a ball trough area. In the gameplay run Start raised the enable 23 and the ROM kicked the outhole, repeated the kick 2.09 s later while 10 stayed closed, and after the drain kicked 6.18 s later, once the bonus count had run; with 10 held from power-up and no game started it never fired.
mechanisms.label: Outhole kicker and shooter lane

mechanisms.behavior: IPDB: "Shooter channel has elevated skill shot to drop ball to a kicker which propels ball into play." The plunged ball climbs the elevated shooter channel past the Shuttle switches 5K (30, topmost), 25K (29, upper), 100K (28) and 25K (27, lower) and drops into the Shuttle 10K kickbig (26, 5647-12133-01), from which the Ball Shooter Kickbig (3, AE-24-900; B-11051-R Shooter Lane Kickbig on a B-11052 mounting) kicks it into play. In the gameplay run the ROM fired 3 1.07 s after 26 closed, and with 26 held from power-up it fired every 3.1-3.3 s. The retained table models the channel with the triggers sw26-sw30 in a line on the right and the KSalida kicker below them.
mechanisms.label: Shooter channel skill shot and shooter-lane kickbig

mechanisms.behavior: A single drop target in the centre of the playfield (C-11903-R 1-b Drop Target Opto Assembly; the ROM's C. DROP TARGET), reset by the Drop Target coil (5, AE-23-800). IPDB: "The drop target guards a cellar hole which feeds the scoop." Knocking it down (18 = 1) flashed the Spins Mystery Wheel flasher (9) in the gameplay run; the ROM raised it only once the ball had passed the cellar hole (11) and reached the boomerang kickbig (13), pulsing 5 twice before and twice after the kickbig fired, and again at the start of each later ball.
mechanisms.label: Spook House drop target

mechanisms.behavior: Behind the drop target a cellar hole takes the ball past the Score Spook House switch (11, 5647-12073-01) to the Boomerang Kickbig (13, 5647-12073-09), from which the kickbig coil (4, AE-26-1500; B-11051-R Boomerang Kickbig on a B-11052 mounting) kicks it round the B-11984 Boomerang Loop Assembly. The three #1251 Boomerang Flashers (15) light the loop. In the gameplay run 11 spun the Mystery Wheel (13 and 14 from 63.11 to 63.83 s); with the ball held on 13 the ROM flashed 15 eight times, pulsed the drop-target reset twice and fired 4 5.25 s after 13 closed. With 13 held from power-up it fired 4 every 1.55-1.67 s. Service bulletin SS52 (October 1988) places the Spookhouse Ramp at the left middle of the playfield, secured to the bottom of the playfield below the Spookhouse entrance hole, with a cushion plate (A-12222) inside under the entrance, and adds a Ramp Support Bracket (A-12407) at its end against breakage. The retained table kicks the ball from its sw13 kicker.
mechanisms.label: Spook House cellar hole and boomerang kickbig

mechanisms.behavior: IPDB lists a "Rotating playfield Ferris wheel" among the notable features and a Ferris Wheel toy, and notes that "The Ferris wheel on the playfield carries the ball for a portion of its rotation." The C-11900 Ferris Wheel/Motor Assembly stands at the top left of the playfield (the retained table's RedWheel); the parts manual lists the Ferris wheel (03-8124) and its cover, turned through a drive belt (03-8145) and pulley (03-8086) by the 14-7941-3 motor of the B-11571-2 Motor Assembly. A relay (5580-12145-01 on the C-11902-1 relay board, solenoid 16) switches the motor; the ball enters at the Ferris Wheel Entrance switch (17, 5647-12073-10). The matrix has no position switch, so the ROM runs the motor without feedback. At power-up the ROM ran the motor from 2.33 to 11.77 s; in the gameplay run it ran it from Start until 9.5 s after the last switch closure and restarted it with the next closure. The retained table turns its RedWheel primitive one degree per FWTimer tick while 16 is on, opens FerrisBlockedWall in four angle windows per turn, and carries a ball that reaches Trigger2 on an arc (lines 711-723 and 755-779). Service bulletin SS50 (July 1988) traces a wheel that does not turn properly to an over-lubricated belt and pulleys slipping, names a white pulley, a metal Ferris wheel bracket, a ball-support bar under the wheel and a two-cavity power plug on the motor. How the physical wheel takes and releases the ball is not printed in the manuals or bulletins.
mechanisms.label: Rotating Ferris wheel

mechanisms.behavior: IPDB: "Mechanical backbox animation (ferris wheel revolves)." The parts manual's Mystery Wheel Carousel Assembly (C-12036) is a carousel wheel (03-8161) on a motor and connector assembly (B-12088) with a stepper motor control assembly (D-12045), the Mystery Wheel Opto Positioner board that carries the opto interruptor module (5490-10159-00, Opto 1) and transistors Q1-Q9; service bulletin SS47 lists its D-12046 subassembly and draws its schematic. The CPU's outputs 13 and 14 reach the board as two logic inputs (input A and input B), each steering one winding of the two-winding stepper motor through a comparator-driven transistor bridge, so their levels, not pulses, set the motor's phase; which output feeds which input is not printed (the Solenoid Table prints their part as 14-7948/D-12045). The opto reports at switch 41, and the sixteen lamps 33-48 sit round the wheel at 22.5-degree steps. The manual's Mystery Wheel Test (08) shows the last known position on the player 2 display, the home state ("H") and the step count (1-200, up to 256 with a failed home switch) on player 4, and the error count on player 3; the wheel stops on the next counterclockwise position when the home switch works. In the retained runs the ROM raised 13 and 14 together, dropped each briefly in turn while stepping, counted to 256 and reported errors with 41 held at either level, showed "H" only with 41 at 0, and restarted its count on a rising edge of 41. In the gameplay run the Score Spook House switch (11) held 13 and 14 on together for 0.72 s. The retained script models the wheel as a cvpmMech stepper (Sol1 14, Sol2 13; .Length = 200 and .Steps = 360, so pinned mech.c wraps its position at 200 and reports it on a 360-position scale) with 41 closed over reported positions 0-180; the physical home flag's width and the motor's steps per turn are not printed.
mechanisms.label: Backbox Mystery Wheel

mechanisms.behavior: Three jet bumpers (B-9414-1 above the playfield, B-9415-1 coil assembly with the AE-23-800 coil beneath it, SW-11A-37 switches): Left (17, switch 60), Right (19, switch 61) and Bottom (21, switch 62), special solenoids 1, 3 and 5. The driver maps no special-solenoid switch, so in PinMAME the ROM fires each coil after reading its switch; the gameplay run showed each pair.
mechanisms.label: Three jet bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two B-9463 kicker arm assemblies with AE-26-1500 coils (the parts manual): Left (18, scoring switch 63) and Right (20, scoring switch 64), special solenoids 2 and 4. The Switches list footnotes a paired kicker actuating switch (A-4834-H; B-8734-1) with no matrix address. In PinMAME the ROM fires each coil after reading its scoring switch, as the gameplay run showed.
mechanisms.label: Left and right kickers (slingshots)

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower flippers (C-11626-L-4 and C-11626-R-4, FL 11630-50VDC coils) fired from the cabinet Flipper Buttons (SW-10A-48) through the flipper circuit, so no Sol. No. is printed and PinMAME fabricates 45-48 from the buttons at public 82 and 84. Each flipper has a Flipper Lane Change switch (57 left, B-9951-1; 58 right, B-9951) whose drawing balloon points at the flipper; core_updateSw copies them from 84 and 82.
mechanisms.label: Two flippers with lane-change switches

mechanisms.behavior: The clear Comet ramp has an entry switch (31, SW-1A-171) and a scoring switch (32, 5647-12133-04) with RIDE THE COMET (8) on the ramp, while the COMET value lamps 27-32 stand above the rear rail; the clear Cyclone ramp has a scoring switch (34, 5647-12133-07). IPDB counts two ramps. Service bulletin SS49 (July 1988) adds a red post (03-8044-9) and a 2" rubber ring (23-6305) stretched between two red posts by the "Ken's Vending" plastic, to stop balls sticking between the playfield plastic and the Cyclone ramp; machines built or serviced after it carry them. The retained script tilts a switch-wire primitive at 32 and 34.
mechanisms.label: Comet and Cyclone ramps

mechanisms.label: Ducks, Ball Toss, top lanes, outlanes and rubber switches

mechanisms.behavior: The A/C Select Relay (12) on the D-11813 Aux Power Driver Board switches each of the eight switched drivers (Q22-Q25, Q30-Q33) between its A load, while it is released, and its C load, while it is energized. Pinned PinMAME publishes the C loads separately at 25-32.

physical.notes: Solenoid Table row 01A ("Outhole Kicker", type Switched, part AE-23-800). Switched pair 01A/01C on driver Q33: the A load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) released and the C load with it energized (the manual's A/C relay note). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 1 and the C load at 25. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 01 while the player 1 and 2 displays show "OUTHOLE". In the gameplay run, with the ball held on 10, Start (3) raised the enable 23 and the ROM kicked the outhole at 15.58 s and again 2.09 s later, when the scenario opened 10; after the drain at 94.08 s it kicked 6.18 s later. With 10 held from power-up and no game started (run boot-held) it never fired, and after the tilted ball drained with 10 held it kicked every 2.04-2.06 s. Retained script: SolCallback(1) = "OutholeKick" (line 127), which kicks the Outhole kicker (lines 146-151). Placement: the retained table's Outhole, which the script binds to this address.

Solenoid Table row 13 ("Mystery Wheel (b) Coil B", type Contrld, part 14-7948/D-12045). The Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Mystery Wheel (bb) Coil A" with no part. Every controlled output 9-16 shows one 50 ms pulse about 0.26 s after power-up, before the ROM initializes PIA0; it is a property of the port, not a drive. One of the two stepper outputs of the backbox Mystery Wheel, with 14; the drive leaves through the backbox connector board (6J2). The Solenoid Table's part cell prints 14-7948/D-12045, and the parts manual lists D-12045 as the Mystery Wheel Opto Positioner board ("Control Assy, Stepper Motor" in the C-12036 Carousel Assembly), which carries transistors Q1-Q9 and the home opto. Service bulletin SS47's schematic draws that board taking two logic inputs, input A and input B, each steering one winding of the two-winding stepper motor; which of 13 and 14 reaches which input is not printed. The Solenoid Table prints 13 as Coil B and 14 as Coil A, while the Solenoids/Flashers list prints 13 as Coil A and 14 as Coil B. The letter decides which winding each output steers, and so the wheel's direction for a given phase sequence; the label follows the Solenoid Table, which carries the wiring. The retained script's stepper model (cvpmMech with vpmMechStepSol, .Sol1 = 14 and .Sol2 = 13, lines 75-77) does not settle the letters: pinned mech.c moves a two-step-solenoid mech whenever either input changes (dir = sol != last), so swapping the two slots gives the same motion. The playfield connection cell "6J2-3 (B'box Conn Bd)" is printed for 13 and "6J2-4" for 14. See the Mystery Wheel mechanism. In the Mystery Wheel Test (runs wheel-test-*) the ROM raised 13 and 14 together and, while the wheel stepped, dropped each for single updates of about 17 ms in an interleaved pattern; in the gameplay run, after the Score Spook House switch (11) closed, it held 13 and 14 on together from 63.11 to 63.83 s. The stepper board takes them as two logic inputs, each steering one motor winding (service bulletin SS47), so a recreation reads them as levels, not as coil pulses; PinMAME's published solenoid state is too coarse to give the phase sequence. The Coil Test skips its step. Retained script: the stepper cvpmMech mWheelMech's second phase, .Sol2 = 13 (lines 71-83), turning the backglass MysteryWheel image.
